Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 96, verses 1–3:

Surat al-Alaq is Meccan. [Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several chains from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The first thing revealed of the Qur'an in Mecca was (Read in the name of your Lord who created)." See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/560–562.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾. Most of the commentators hold that this surah is the first surah revealed of the Qur'an, and that the first thing revealed was the first five verses of it, up to His words: "what he did not know."

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] informed us: Yahya ibn Bukayr informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, from A'isha, the Mother of the Believers, that she said: "The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was begun in revelation was the true dream in sleep. He never had a dream but it came like the break of dawn. Then solitude became dear to him, and he would seclude himself in the cave of Hira, where he would engage in tahannuth, which is worship, for many nights before returning to his family. He would take provisions for that, and then return to Khadija, and take provisions for the like of it, until the Truth came to him while he was in the cave of Hira. The Angel came to him and said: 'Read.' He said: 'I am not a reader.' He said: 'He seized me and pressed me until I reached my limit, then released me and said: "Read." I said: "I am not a reader."' [He said: 'He seized me] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "b".]] and pressed me a second time until I reached my limit, then released me and said: 'Read.' I said: 'I am not a reader.' He seized me and pressed me a third time [until I reached my limit] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "b".]], then released me and said: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous﴾. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned with it, his heart trembling, and entered upon Khadija bint Khuwaylid, and said: 'Wrap me up, wrap me up!' So they wrapped him until the fright left him. Then he said to Khadija: 'What is happening to me?' and he told her the news, and said: 'I fear for myself.' Khadija said: 'Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You join the ties of kinship, bear the burdens of others, earn for the destitute, entertain the guest, and help in the calamities of the truth.' Then Khadija set out with him and brought him to Waraqa ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza, the cousin of Khadija, who had become a Christian in the pre-Islamic period. He used to write the Arabic script and would write from the Injil (Gospel) in Arabic whatever Allah willed him to write. He was an old man who had gone blind. Khadija said to him: 'O cousin, listen to what your nephew says.' Waraqa said to him: 'O nephew, what do you see?' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed him of what he had seen. Waraqa said to him: 'This is the namus (divine confidant) that Allah sent down to Musa. Would that I were young in those days! Would that I were alive when your people expel you.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Will they expel me?' He said: 'Yes. No one has come with the like of what you have brought except that he was opposed. If your day reaches me, I will support you with a mighty support.' Then Waraqa did not remain long before he died, and the revelation paused." [al-Bukhari narrated it in the Book of the Beginning of Revelation, chapter "How the beginning of revelation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was": 1/23.]

Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated this hadith in another place of his book, from Yahya ibn Bukayr with this chain, and said: "Abdullah ibn Muhammad informed me: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, [and] al-Zuhri said: 'Urwa informed me, from A'isha,' and he mentioned the hadith, and said: '"Read in the name of your Lord who created" until he reached "what he did not know."' He added at its end: 'The revelation paused for a period until the Prophet (ﷺ) grew sad, as has reached us, a sadness that drove him many times until he would throw himself from the peaks of high mountains. Whenever he reached the summit of a mountain to cast himself down from it, Jibril appeared to him and said: "O Muhammad, you are truly the Messenger of Allah." His heart would be calmed by that and his soul at rest, and he would return. When the pause of the revelation lengthened on him, he would set out for the same purpose, and whenever he reached the summit of a mountain, Jibril would appear to him and say to him the like of that.'" [al-Bukhari narrated it in the Book of Interpretation (Ta'bir), chapter "The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was begun in revelation was the true dream": 12/351–352, and Muslim in the Book of Faith, chapter "The beginning of revelation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," no. (160): 1/139–142.]

Ahmad ibn Abdan informed us: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us: Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Warraq informed us: Makki ibn Abdan informed us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr informed us: Sufyan informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, from A'isha, who said: "The first surah revealed was His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: 'Read in the name of your Lord.'" [al-Tabari narrated it: 30/252. al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/529. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/561) added its attribution to Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.]

Abu Ubayda said: its figurative sense is "Read the name of your Lord," meaning that the bа' (in bismi) is superfluous, and the meaning is: "Mention His name." He was commanded to begin the reading with the name of Allah [out of good manners] [[In "b": tadiban (with good manners).]].

﴿who created﴾. Al-Kalbi said: it means the creatures. Then he explained it, saying: ﴿created man﴾, meaning the son of Adam, ﴿from a clinging substance﴾, which is the plural of alaqah (a clot).

﴿Read﴾: He repeated it for emphasis, then began anew, saying: ﴿and your Lord is the Most Generous﴾. Al-Kalbi said: He is the Forbearing toward the ignorance of His servants and does not hasten to punish them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 96, verses 4–10:

﴿Who taught by the pen﴾, meaning writing and script.

﴿He taught man what he did not know﴾ of the kinds of guidance and clarification. It is also said: He taught Adam all the names. And it is said: "man" here refers to Muhammad (ﷺ), as evidenced by His words: ﴿And He taught you what you did not know﴾ [al-Nisa: 113].

﴿Nay﴾, truly, ﴿indeed, man transgresses﴾, that is, he goes beyond his limit and acts arrogantly toward his Lord.

﴿That﴾ because ﴿he sees himself as self-sufficient﴾, that is, when he sees himself as rich. Al-Kalbi said: he rises from one station to another in clothing, food and other things.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl. Whenever he acquired wealth, he increased his clothing, his mount and his food, and that was his transgression.

﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾, that is, the ultimate place of return in the Hereafter. [“al-Ruj'a” is a verbal noun on the pattern fu'la.] [[The text between the brackets is omitted in "A".]]

﴿Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays?﴾ It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, who forbade the Prophet (ﷺ) from prayer. [[See al-Tabari: 30/254; Ibn Kathir: 4/529.]]

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us, 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Mu'adh and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Qaysi narrated to us, both saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us from his father, Na'im ibn Abi Hind narrated to me, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: Abu Jahl said: "Does Muhammad rub his face (in the dust) among you?" It was said: "Yes." He said: "By al-Lat and al-'Uzza, if I see him doing that, I will certainly step on his neck and rub his face in the dust." He said: So he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was praying, intending to step on his neck. But suddenly they saw him retreating on his heels, protecting himself with his hands. It was said to him: "What is wrong with you, O Abu al-Hakam?" He said: "Between me and him there is a trench of fire, and terror, and wings." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If he had come near me, the angels would have snatched him limb from limb." He said: Then Allah revealed — we do not know whether in the hadith of Abu Hurayra or in something that reached him — "Nay, indeed, man transgresses, that he sees himself as self-sufficient. Indeed, to your Lord is the return. Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays?" and the verses that follow. [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of the Attributes of the Hypocrites, chapter on His words "Indeed, man transgresses," no. 2797: 4/2154.]]

The meaning of "Have you seen" (ara'ayta) here is to express wonder at the addressee. He repeated this expression for emphasis:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 96, verses 11–16:

﴿Have you considered: if he is upon guidance﴾, meaning the servant who is forbidden, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿or enjoins righteousness﴾, meaning with sincere devotion (ikhlas) and monotheism (tawhid).

﴿Have you considered: if he denies and turns away﴾, meaning Abu Jahl, ﴿and turns away﴾ from faith.

The structure of the verse is: "Have you considered the one who forbids a servant when he prays [and the forbidden one, in "B": he is] upon guidance, enjoining righteousness, while the forbidder denies and turns away from faith?" How strange is this! ﴿Does he not know﴾, meaning Abu Jahl, ﴿that Allah sees﴾ that, so that He will recompense him for it.

﴿No!﴾ He does not know that. ﴿If he does not desist﴾ from harming [His Prophet, in "B": Muhammad] (ﷺ) and denying him, ﴿We will surely seize him by the forelock﴾, meaning we will certainly take hold of his forelock and drag him into the Fire, as He said: "They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet" [al-Rahman: 41]. It is said: "safa'tu bi-l-shay'" means when I took hold of it and pulled it with a strong pull. And "al-nasiyah" is the hair of the front of the head. Then He said, as an apposition: ﴿a lying, sinful forelock﴾, meaning its owner is a liar and a sinner. Ibn Abbas said: When Abu Jahl forbade the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from prayer, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rebuked him. Abu Jahl said: "Do you rebuke me, O Muhammad? You know that I have more people in this valley than you do." Then he said: "By Allah, I will fill this valley against you, if you wish, with horses and men."

**Al-Baghawi, Ma'alim al-Tanzil (Commentary on surah 96, verses 17–19):**

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Then let him call his assembly﴾, that is, his people and his kinsmen; that is, let him seek help from them.

﴿We will call the guards of Hell (al-zabaniyah)﴾. It is the plural of zibniy, derived from al-zibn, which means pushing. Ibn 'Abbas said: he means the guards of Hell (zabaniyat Jahannam); they were named so because they push the people of the Fire into it. Al-Zajjaj said: they are the harsh, severe angels. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Had he called his assembly, the guards of Allah would have seized him."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/256.]] Then He said: ﴿No!﴾, meaning the matter is not as Abu Jahl supposes. ﴿Do not obey him﴾ in abandoning the prayer. ﴿And prostrate yourself﴾, that is, pray to Allah, ﴿and draw near﴾ to Allah.

Abu Tahir 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Qashani informed us: Abu 'Umar al-Qasim ibn Ja'far al-Hashimi informed us: Abu 'Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Lu'lu'i narrated to us: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Salih, Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn al-Sarraj and Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, saying: Wahb informed us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from 'Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, that he heard Abu Salih Dhakwan narrating from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so increase supplication [therein]."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Salat, bab al-du'a fi al-ruku' wa al-sujud: 1/420, and Muslim in al-Salat, bab ma yuqal fi al-ruku' wa al-sujud, no. (482): 1/350; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 3/151.]]

**Al-Baghawi, Ma'alim al-Tanzil (Commentary on surah 96, verses 17–19):**

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Then let him call his assembly﴾, that is, his people and his kinsmen; that is, let him seek help from them.

﴿We will call the guards of Hell (al-zabaniyah)﴾. It is the plural of zibniy, derived from al-zibn, which means pushing. Ibn 'Abbas said: he means the guards of Hell (zabaniyat Jahannam); they were named so because they push the people of the Fire into it. Al-Zajjaj said: they are the harsh, severe angels. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Had he called his assembly, the guards of Allah would have seized him."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/256.]] Then He said: ﴿No!﴾, meaning the matter is not as Abu Jahl supposes. ﴿Do not obey him﴾ in abandoning the prayer. ﴿And prostrate yourself﴾, that is, pray to Allah, ﴿and draw near﴾ to Allah.
